title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 303 (Appeals from orders made before commencement of Act)

content.overview: Any appeal against an order made under the Companies Act, 1956, before the commencement of this Act, which is pending, continues as if this Act had not been passed; the appellate forum and procedure remain those under the 1956 Act for such pending appeals.
content.glance: Pending appeals against 1956-Act orders continue under the old Act's appellate machinery.
content.study: Section 303 is a transitional provision. Appeals against orders made under the Companies Act, 1956 that were pending at the commencement of the 2013 Act continue as if the 2013 Act had not been passed. The appellate forum and procedure for those pending appeals remain those applicable under the 1956 Act.

examples.title: Pending appeal
examples.body: An appeal against a 1956-Act winding-up order was pending when the 2013 Act commenced. Under s. 303 that appeal continues under the 1956-Act appellate route.
